response.reason: The cited clause, Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Art. 26(3), establishes the requirement that if the country of origin or place of provenance of a food is given and it is not the same as that of its primary ingredient, the origin of the primary ingredient must also be given or indicated as different. The verdict turns on this requirement, stating that since both the product and its primary ingredient have the same origin (Poland), no additional statement is required. This is a correct application of the cited clause, which only imposes an obligation when the origins differ.
